head: be87ad5721901f90b507bb9f8b3ba5f9454295b0
scope: Current uncommitted working tree, including the site performance work, existing employee-editing / AI-exclusion changes, and the production review fixes.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Removed physical-row fingerprints and the separate initial version query. The page hashes its already-loaded data. Polls run the same filtered page readers and return only the hash. Visible changes, deletions and due-time transitions invalidate it; unrelated edits and physical row rewrites do not.

initialBatchReaderQueries.excludes: unchanged authentication and catalog user lookup

resolvedFindings.correctness: Exact filters, repeated values, metrics and page bounds are retained. Tokens represent the values actually rendered, so an edit after a page read cannot be acknowledged without being displayed. Existing draft, hidden-tab and pending-navigation guards remain active.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Upgraded to patched Zod, enforced a 1 MiB byte limit before parsing interactive dashboard mutation requests, and limited validation responses to eight issues of at most 512 characters each. Streamed bytes are counted regardless of Content-Length; geometric buffering avoids retaining arbitrarily many small chunks.
resolvedFindings.compatibility: The supported 20,000 selected IDs plus assignment notes still pass. Retained nonstandard PostgreSQL/provider UUIDs keep the old acceptance contract through z.guid(); dictionary schemas were migrated explicitly. Empty inference bodies, UTF-8 and BOM handling remain supported.

dependencies.sdkVerification: Actual upgraded OpenAI SDK exercised against a stubbed fetch transport for both structured-output requests and rate-limit propagation without retries.

validation.browserCounting: Counted unique file/test titles across the runs; repeat executions are not added. The broad run passed 306 tests; its outdated catalog-refresh expectation passed after updating the contract. Targeted batch/navigation/boundary checks supply 21 additional distinct cases.
testCorrections: New refresh counters initially included Next.js link prefetches. Traces confirmed prefetch headers; corrected counters exclude them and still require a real refresh after visible edits.

The previous manual catalog test expected a refresh for an assignment note not shown in that catalog. It now requires no refresh for that note, then verifies a visible batch creation and the note changing in the legacy detail view.
validation.buildEnvironment: The restricted sandbox returned empty output from Next.js detached TypeScript subprocesses. The unmodified production build succeeded outside that sandbox; type checking was not disabled.

readOnlyProviderPayloadCompatibility.method: Validate up to 100 recent retained provider payloads using the previous schema with Zod 3 and the current schema with patched Zod 4. No payloads or identifiers are recorded.

performance.method: Three-way reader comparison in one enforced READ ONLY snapshot: original pre-optimization readers, rejected fingerprint implementation, and fixed page-data tokens. Rotating execution order across three rounds. Excludes unchanged authentication/users/rendering; catalog hashing uses an empty people list equally for timing. No identifiers or record contents recorded.
performance.interpretation: The fixed AI detail median was 327 ms versus 353 ms before optimization. AI catalog was 509 ms versus 632 ms. Timings vary with cache state and database/network load; these three samples per version are not end-to-end latency or a production concurrency test.

checks: No extra initial token query or global table fingerprint remains.
Hashes are computed from displayed data; object keys and filter-option arrays have stable order.
Polling preserves filter values without trimming exact-match criteria, including repeated filters and page bounds.
Older-row edits, deletions, legacy batches, expired follow-ups, no-result pages and admin authorization are covered.
Polling does not replace drafts, run concurrently in a tab, or wait for provider reconciliation.
Oversized arrays stop before element validation; byte limits cannot be bypassed by missing or false Content-Length.
Allocation guards, ownership, revision conflicts, employee/admin attribution, Kanban moves and data preservation passed regression checks.
Only the intended dependency versions changed; the production audit is clean.

remainingLimits: Polling still reads the scoped page and whole-batch aggregates every 30 seconds. Very large batches or many simultaneous viewers can require further capacity work.
Provider network behavior was tested with stubs; no live calls or production deployment were performed. The read-only payload comparison sampled 100 retained executions.
The assessment applies to this tested working tree; it is not a guarantee of zero defects under every production condition.

followUpReview.testEvidence: Rechecked the completed build, typecheck, test and audit records against the unchanged tested source. No full-suite rerun was needed for this review.
reviewedAreas: Allocation preview cache invalidation, full-selection hash verification under the ownership lock, and request replay.
Employee/admin authorization, audit attribution, revision conflicts, queued confirmations, and preservation of drafts.
Batch polling filter parity, displayed-data tokens, deletion and due-time invalidation, and independence from provider synchronization.
Lazy transcript authorization for the exact execution/provider call and cancellation of obsolete requests.
Consolidated query semantics, shared-number exclusions, request-size boundaries, dependency compatibility, and corrected regression assertions.
